actualSourceFetches.pageTitle: IRAS | Reporting Employee Earnings (IR8A, App 8A/8B)
actualSourceFetches.bodyExcerpt: IRAS | Reporting Employee Earnings (IR8A, App 8A/8B) You are using an outdated browser. Please upgrade your browser to improve your experience. Employers are required by law (S68(2) of the Income Tax Act) to prepare Form IR8A and Appendix 8A, Appendix 8B or Form IR8S (where applicable prior to YA 2026) for employees who are employed in Singapore by 1 Mar of the year after the year the income is derived by the employee. Employers do not need to submit the hardcopy forms to IRAS. On this page: Tax forms for employers Form Name Description Guides/FAQs Form IR8A (DOCX, 69KB) This form must be completed for ALL employees: Full-time resident employee Part-time resident employee Non-resident employee including those who are based overseas and are required to render service in Singapore during the year (exclude details of employment income where clearance has been filed) Company director (including a non-resident director) Board members receiving Board/Committee Member Fees Pensioner Employee who has left the organisation but was in receipt of income in the reporting year (e.g., stock options gains) Note: For employees’ overseas posting not incidental to Singapore employment, please note that it is not compulsory for employers to state the amount of overseas employment income in the Form IR8A. Employers participating in AIS are only required to select ‘“Income from Overseas Employment”’ under ‘"Exempt/Remission Income"’ indicator. Explanatory notes on Form IR8A & Appendix 8A (PDF, 372KB) Appendix 8A (DOC, 90KB) This form must be completed for employees who were provided with benefits-in-kind. Explanatory notes on Form IR8A & Appendix 8A (PDF, 372KB) Appendix 8B (DOC, 92KB) This form must be completed for employees who derived gains or profits from Employee Stock Option (ESOP) Plans or other forms of Employee Share Ownership (ESOW) Plans. Explanatory notes on Appendix 8B (PDF, 201KB) View copies of the forms for YA 2026 . Employers are responsible for reporting the employment income of all individuals who have worked for them. If an employee has changed jobs during the year, each employer is required to submit income information for the period the employee was under its employment. This applies to all employers with whom the employee has had an employment contract, regardless of the duration of employment. In cases where employees are transferred from one entity to another entity due to a change of constitution of the employer (e.g., a company restructuring or merger) during the year, the employer may either: Submit information under the respective entity according to the contract periods, or Combine the employees’ employment income information under the new entity. Employers under Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income Employers specified under paragraph 4 of the gazette (PDF, 204 KB) must submit their employees’ income information to IRAS electronically by 1 Mar of the year after the year the income is derived by the employee. The information submitted by employers will be pre-filled in employees' electronic Income Tax Returns. AIS employers do not need to issue hardcopy Form IR8A and the appendices to their employees. Learn more on Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income . Employers not under Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income Employers who are not under the AIS will have to provide the hardcopy Form IR8A and appendices (where applicable) to their employees by 1 Mar of the year after the year the income is derived by the employee so that the employees could file their Income Tax Returns with the information. Employers need not submit the forms to IRAS. FAQs Do employers need to fill in ‘Date of Commencement’ and ‘Date of Cessation’ field(s) in the Form IR8A? Employers will need to provide the date of commencement if the employee commenced employment in the year or before 1 Jan 1969. Fill in the ‘Date of Cessation’ if your employee ceased employment in the year. To fill in the Form IR8A for 2025 (Year of Assessment 2026): 1. If employee joined on 1 Dec 1968 but did not cease employment, the employer should fill in ‘Date of Commencement’ as ‘01/12/1968’ and leave the ‘Date of Cessation’ as blank 2. If employee joined on 15 Jan 2025 and ceased employment on 20 Aug 2025, the employer should fill in the ‘Date of Commencement’ as ‘15/01/2025’ and ‘Date of Cessation as ‘20/08/2025’ 3. If the employee joined on 25 Feb 2017 and ceased employment on 1 Nov 2025, the employer should leave the ‘Date of Commencement’ as blank and fill in the ‘Date of Cessation’ as ‘01/11/2025’ Must the employer complete the ‘Bank Salary is credited to’ field in the Form IR8A? If the employee's salary is credited to a bank account, employers will need to indicate the bank name (e.g., POSB). However, indicate as ‘Others’ if the salary payment was made in cash or cheque in the Form IR8A. Pages Employers

actualSourceFetches.bodyExcerpt: IRAS | Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA) for Foreign Individuals You are using an outdated browser. Please upgrade your browser to improve your experience. What is Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)? A Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA) allows foreign users to access selected government and private sector digital services in Singapore, including personal and corporate tax services on myTax Portal. Who needs to apply for an SFA? a) You must apply for an SFA with IRAS if you are a foreign individual without a Singapore Government-issued ID, and you need to transact with us digitally for Individual and/or Property Tax matters. This includes: - Singaporeans/Singapore PRs who have renounced their citizenship/Permanent Residence - Former FIN holders who have cancelled their work pass - Foreigners with an existing IRAS Tax reference number (e.g., A1234567A) For Corppass users (including Tax Agents) handling business tax matters, an SFA will be issued automatically by Corppass when you apply for a Corppass user account. In this case, there is no need to apply for an SFA separately with IRAS. How to Apply for an SFA? Complete the application form to apply for an SFA. Before you begin, please ensure you have the following prepared: a. Your National ID (e.g., Malaysian IC, National Identity Card). If unavailable, a passport document with at least 6 months validity. b. A valid email address. Your SFA ID will be sent to this email upon successful processing. - Ensure you can access the email inbox before proceeding. - Verify that the email address has not been used for previous SFA applications or registered with Singpass. c. Your existing/previous tax reference number with IRAS, if any (e.g., A1234567A, G1234567X, S1234567D). The new SFA account has to be activated within 90 days from date of issuance. Otherwise, the account will be terminated by Singpass, and you will need to reapply for a new SFA account with IRAS. Steps to activate SFA Step 1: Once your SFA application is successful, you will receive an email from Singpass with the subject "Registration of Singpass Account (Foreign User)" at your registered email address with the following: • System generated SFA User ID (e.g. Y1234567A) • Instructions to download Singpass app • Steps to complete a one-time setup using the SFA User ID and the details as per your SFA application Step 2: Download the Singpass mobile app and click on "Start here" to setup your SFA. Setup must be completed within 90 days from the date of the email. Step 3: Congratulations! Upon the setup of your SFA, you may login to myTax Portal the next working day . FAQs A. SFA Application 1. I have renounced my Singapore citizenship/Permanent Residence or my FIN has expired. Which tax reference number should I use in the Singpass Foreign Account (SFA) application form? You should still enter the NRIC or FIN that was previously issued to you when filling out the application form, even if it is no longer valid. 2. Can both my spouse and I use the same email address when applying for our Singpass Foreign User Accounts? No, each applicant must use a unique email address that was not used for Singpass or IRAS Unique Account when applying for their own Singpass Foreign Account (SFA). You and your spouse will need to provide separate email addresses for your individual applications. 3. What can I expect after submitting my SFA application? You can expect to receive the activation email within 10 working days from Singpass. Please do check your email’s junk or spam folder as well. If you still do not receive the activation email, you may contact Singpass for assistance. 4. Do I have to re-apply for a SFA with IRAS to login myTax Portal if I have been issued with a SFA by another agency? SFA can be issued by different SFA organisations (e.g. Corppass). SFA can only be used to access the digital services of the SFA organisation that issued the account to you. If you have a SFA ID issued by another SFA organisation and you wish to access IRASʼ digital services for Individual and/or Property Tax matters, please complete the application form and indicate your existing SFA ID (e.g. Y1234567A). You also need to attach the same Foreign ID document (e.g. Passport document or National ID) that was submitted to the other SFA organisation. B. Unable to log in to myTax Portal 1. I do not recall my SFA User ID i.e., Y-series no. You may retrieve your SFA User ID (e.g., Y1234567C) at this Singpass page . 2. I am unable to access myTax Portal after setting up my SFA. Please allow one working day for the system to sync your details before logging in. 3. I am not able to log into myTax Portal using the issued SFA. Please consider the following: a. SFA Activation: Ensure that you have activated your SFA within 90 days from the date of issuance. Otherwise, the account will be terminated by Singpass and you will need to resubmit a new application with us. b. Validity of Official Document: Check that the official document used for your SFA application is not expired nor due to expire within the next six months. If it has expired or is nearing expiry, submit a new application with your renewed document. When applying, select "Updating of expiring/expired official identification document(s)" as your Reason for Application.

The Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS) is a voluntary scheme to encourage individuals to save for retirement, over and above their CPF savings. Contributions to SRS are eligible for tax relief. Investment returns are tax-free before withdrawal and only 50% of the withdrawals from SRS are taxable at retirement. Find out more on Tax on SRS withdrawals . You can only have 1 SRS account at any point in time and contributions to the SRS account must be made by ^ 31 Dec 2025 to qualify for SRS Relief (subject to overall personal income tax relief cap of $80,000) for the Year of Assessment (YA) 2026. Opening SRS accounts with more than 1 SRS operator is an offence and there may be penalty imposed. ^ You may check with your SRS bank operator about the cut-off date for SRS contributions. On this page: Opening an SRS account Who is eligible to open an SRS account Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents (SPRs) and foreigners who: Are at least 18 years of age; Are not an undischarged bankrupt; Are not having a mental disorder; and are capable of managing yourself and your affairs; Does not already have an SRS account (including one that has been suspended) with the same or another operator; Does not have a pending application with another SRS operator to open an SRS account; and Does not previously have an SRS account with the same or another SRS operator and all the monies in the account have been withdrawn - i. On medical grounds; or ii. On or after reaching the statutory retirement age prevailing at the time of your first contribution. How to open an SRS account SRS accounts are managed by 3 bank operators: DBS Group Holdings Ltd Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) Ltd United Overseas Bank (UOB) Ltd You may approach the banks listed above to open an SRS account (you will need to acknowledge/confirm that you do not have another SRS account with other SRS operators before proceeding with the application) and start to contribute. Documents required for opening an SRS account: Identity card/Passport Completed Declaration Form for SRS (For Foreigners) (DOC, 220KB) Changing of SRS bank operator You may change the SRS bank operator of your SRS account by obtaining the “Transfer of Account Form” from the new SRS operator, who will then liaise with your existing operator to effect the transfer. SRS contributions and tax relief All SRS contributions must be made by 31 Dec of the year or as required by your SRS operator, to be eligible for SRS tax relief in the following YA following the year of contribution. You are advised to check with your SRS bank operator for the cut-off date for SRS contributions. For each YA, a personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs claimed (including relief on SRS contributions). There will be no refund for SRS contributions made. Please evaluate whether you would benefit from tax relief before making your SRS contributions. Making SRS contributions You and/or your employer (on your behalf) may contribute at any time, and as often as you like , subject to the maximum SRS contribution for the year. Contributions must be made in cash. However, SRS contributions cannot be made if you start withdrawing from your SRS account: At or after the statutory retirement age that was prevailing when you made your first SRS contribution; or On medical grounds. Contributions made by your employer to your SRS account on your behalf constitute part of your remuneration. Such contributions are taxable and must be declared by your employer in your Form IR8A for the relevant YA. You will be granted tax relief for such contributions. Yearly maximum SRS contributions Singapore Citizens/Singapore Permanent Residents Foreigners $15,300 $35,700 For foreigners: Annual declaration required by SRS bank operator You are required to declare your foreigner status by submitting the Declaration Form for SRS (For Foreigners) (DOC, 220KB) yearly for the SRS operator to calculate your maximum SRS contribution for the year. Updating SRS Bank Operator Upon Obtaining Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency If you become a Singapore Citizen or SPR during the year, please update the SRS bank operator as your maximum contribution amount will have to be recalculated even if you have already made contributions for that year. The SRS bank operator will re-compute your SRS contribution cap for the year on a pro-rata basis. Penalties may be imposed for excess contributions if a wrongful declaration has been made to the SRS bank operator. For example, if you are a SPR at the time of contribution, it would be incorrect to declare yourself as a foreigner. If you require more information on SRS, you may refer to the SRS booklet available on the Ministry of Finance’s website. Qualifying for SRS tax relief You will be allowed SRS tax relief in the YA following the year of contribution, provided you are a tax resident for that YA. However, a personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs claimed (including relief on SRS contributions). You will not be allowed SRS tax relief if: Your SRS account is suspended as at 31 Dec of the year of contribution; or The amount of such contribution is withdrawn from your SRS account in the same year of contribution. On this page:

A DTA between Singapore and another jurisdiction allows reduction or exemption of tax on certain types of income if it is earned in one jurisdiction by a resident of the other jurisdiction.

How to claim tax relief under the DTA

Non-resident company | Non-resident professional (consultant, trainer, coach, etc.)

Step 1: Check for non-resident’s eligibility for Double Taxation Relief (DTR)



Use the S45 Double Taxation Relief Tax Rate Calculator to check if the non-resident company is eligible for DTR and the applicable tax rate under the DTA.

View DTA for full details of the DTR available.

If DTA does not apply, withhold tax at the prevailing tax rate, file and make payment to IRAS by the due date.

If DTA applies, check the "Double Taxation Relief" box and indicate the applicable tax rate when filing.



Use the DTA Calculator for Non-resident Professional to check if the non-resident professional is eligible for DTR.

View DTA for full details of the DTR available.

If DTA does not apply, withhold tax at the prevailing tax rate, file and make payment to IRAS by the due date.

If DTA applies, check the "Claim for relief under Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement (DTA)" and indicate the applicable tax rate when filing.

Step 2: Obtain supporting document from the non-resident



Certificate of Residence (COR)

• Obtain the COR from the non-resident for each year the DTR is claimed.

• The COR must:

◦ Be certified by the foreign tax authority of the non-resident

◦ Be in English. If the COR is not in English, please obtain an English translated copy

◦ Clearly state that

▪ the non-resident company is a resident of the foreign country/region for DTA purposes and

▪ the year(s) that the COR is applicable for

◦

•

One COR may be accepted for multiple years if the relevant years are clearly stated in the COR.

The specimen format of COR from non-resident (DOCX, 23KB) serves as a guide to the payer on the information required from the foreign tax authority. Foreign tax authorities do not need to follow the specimen COR format but must provide the requisite information.



Signed Form IR586

Obtain Form IR586 signed by the non-resident professional if the tax treaty exemption applies.

Step 3: Submit the document to IRAS by the due date



Upload the scanned COR and translated copy (if applicable) to IRAS as a PDF file, with file size not more than 3MB, by the due date.

The due date is

• 31 Mar of the following year if the claim is for a period in the current calendar year

Example:
You submit a Withholding Tax (WHT) filing in the year 2025, with period of payment between 1 Jan 2025 and 31 Dec 2025.

To claim DTR, you must submit the COR for 2025 to IRAS by 31 Mar 2026.

• Within 3 months from the date of WHT submission if the claim is for preceding calendar years.

Example:
You submit a WHT filing on 30 Jun 2025, with period of payment between 1 Jan 2023 and 31 Dec 2024.

To claim DTR, you must submit CORs for 2023 and 2024 to IRAS by 30 Sep 2025.

DTR may be withdrawn and late payment penalties imposed if the COR is not submitted by the due date.

You do not need to submit the original COR unless requested by IRAS. All documents and records are to be retained for 5 years.



You do not need to submit the signed Form IR586 unless requested by IRAS. All documents and records are to be retained for 5 years.

Request for extension of time to submit COR

You may request for an extension of up to 2 months to submit COR by completing the online form. This is subject to IRAS' approval.

Claim of Relief under the Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement (DTA)

Share:

•

•

•

•

•

•

On this page:

A DTA between Singapore and another jurisdiction allows reduction or exemption of tax on certain types of income if it is earned in one jurisdiction by a resident of the other jurisdiction.

How to claim tax relief under the DTA

Non-resident company | Non-resident professional (consultant, trainer, coach, etc.)

Step 1: Check for non-resident’s eligibility for Double Taxation Relief (DTR)



Use the S45 Double Taxation Relief Tax Rate Calculator to check if the non-resident company is eligible for DTR and the applicable tax rate under the DTA.

View DTA for full details of the DTR available.

If DTA does not apply, withhold tax at the prevailing tax rate, file and make payment to IRAS by the due date.

If DTA applies, check the "Double Taxation Relief" box and indicate the applicable tax rate when filing.



Use the DTA Calculator for Non-resident Professional to check if the non-resident professional is eligible for DTR.

View DTA for full details of the DTR available.

If DTA does not apply, withhold tax at the prevailing tax rate, file and make payment to IRAS by the due date.

If DTA applies, check the "Claim for relief under Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement (DTA)" and indicate the applicable tax rate when filing.

Step 2: Obtain supporting document from the non-resident



Certificate of Residence (COR)

• Obtain the COR from the non-resident for each year the DTR is claimed.

• The COR must:

◦ Be certified by the foreign tax authority of the non-resident

◦ Be in English. If the COR is not in English, please obtain an English translated copy

◦ Clearly state that

▪ the non-resident company is a resident of the foreign country/region for DTA purposes and

▪ the year(s) that the COR is applicable for

◦

•

One COR may be accepted for multiple years if the relevant years are clearly stated in the COR.

The specimen format of COR from non-resident (DOCX, 23KB) serves as a guide to the payer on the information required from the foreign tax authority. Foreign tax authorities do not need to follow the specimen COR format but must provide the requisite information.



Signed Form IR586

Obtain Form IR586 signed by the non-resident professional if the tax treaty exemption applies.

Step 3: Submit the document to IRAS by the due date



Upload the scanned COR and translated copy (if applicable) to IRAS as a PDF file, with file size not more than 3MB, by the due date.

The due date is

• 31 Mar of the following year if the claim is for a period in the current calendar year

Example:
You submit a Withholding Tax (WHT) filing in the year 2025, with period of payment between 1 Jan 2025 and 31 Dec 2025.

To claim DTR, you must submit the COR for 2025 to IRAS by 31 Mar 2026.

• Within 3 months from the date of WHT submission if the claim is for preceding calendar years.

Example:
You submit a WHT filing on 30 Jun 2025, with period of payment between 1 Jan 2023 and 31 Dec 2024.

To claim DTR, you must submit CORs for 2023 and 2024 to IRAS by 30 Sep 2025.

DTR may be withdrawn and late payment penalties imposed if the COR is not submitted by the due date.

You do not need to submit the original COR unless requested by IRAS. All documents and records are to be retained for 5 years.



You do not need to submit the signed Form IR586 unless requested by IRAS. All documents and records are to be retained for 5 years.

Request for extension of time to submit COR

You may request for an extension of up to 2 months to submit COR by completing the online form. This is subject to IRAS' approval.
